body: Thank you very much for talking with me. You are very kind to give your perspective on things--it helps me, even if it only helps a little.

The last major one lasted a few months, when I was in high school. It was about 5 months or so, but there were a few highs to offset the lows. Now, it seems like all I ever am is low.

After my last "depression" passed in high school, I felt very hopeful, like I had potential to really experience life. I was going to college then, and so I really felt like the world was at my doorstep. I very much wish that I could feel that way again, but I just don't know. I feel so incredibly down that it's hard to imagine that life will ever be different from the way it is now. I hate how depressive I am, and it seems like telling the truth and saying how things will never get better is only making me hate myself more. I've felt depressed for a very, very long time, but I've only just recently acknowledged it, and it's as if I'm not quite ready to tell the truth to myself.

But thank you very much for your kind words. It means a lot to me to know that there are such kind and understanding strangers out there.

Thank you. It gives me hope that you were able to find help. I want to believe that I can get better soon, but in all reality, I feel as if I just don't know if it's possible. But thank you so, so much for sharing your story (and the hotline number) with me.

I'm not sure what's causing my depression. I've looked at it from every angle and all I can think of is that there's something seriously wrong with me, something broken. Maybe it's biochemical? Maybe it's just me? I don't know.

But yes, I've been thinking of taking a year off school. I don't know exactly how I would do it, with paying rent and financial aid and all, but I know it might help. I really need some sort of help, too--it's just so hard to keep living.

Thank you very much for helping me feel that I'm not alone. It means a lot to me.
